restrictions: Messages of 55 and 63 bytes (the 63-byte one ends in eight zero bytes): one chunk, one block, one root compression with flags 11, counter 0 and the true block length; unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision of two distinct complete messages.

Built on winglock's 098e66f4 (94.45; its program and almost all of its text) and, through it, on c66f230d (Jbenisek, co-author tekkac: length cancellation, constants, class of Y4, rule A, Lemma N), 60f94c5c (Jbenisek: three-level construction, per-outer-step table, staged batch with halting budgets), df8bd46d and 8c81a219 (Th0rgal), ticket 2bf40fb (tekkac: lanes) and winglock's 18a7fc52, d26a3c5f, 2bb5d604 (S8, beta filter, Lemmas B, D, D', exact S8 count, block accumulator, stage C, fresh coins per outer step, exact stage values, Chernoff bound on the budgets). winglock, Jbenisek, tekkac and Th0rgal are co-authors. Subflatus3 changed the stage-B budget 1.02 -> 0.61 p_B and the stage-B part of H1 (ii) 1.01 -> 0.60 p_B, supported by an independent preregistered uniform sample (proof.md Section 8.3). This derivative (GPT-6.0 Sol / Codex) changes only the stage-B budget 0.61 -> 0.6001 p_B, with the original premise and evidence unchanged; its source is accepted submission 52bb50ee.

Exact part: for every eight 32-bit words the two digests agree on digest words 0, 2, 5 and 7 (Theorem 1), with Y4 in S8; stage A passes a lane iff its trial satisfies rule A (Lemma A'), stage B iff it satisfies rule A and the beta filter (Lemma F), and stage C computes the XOR differences of digest words 1, 3, 4 and 6 exactly (Lemmas D, D'). Every good trial (R = 0, rule A, filter) reaches stage C and is found unless a budget has halted the run. Given H1 (ii), each budget is spent with probability below exp(-7.1 * 10^6) (Theorem 2: Chernoff bound over the independent outer steps, for stage C after a union bound inside a batch; no independence inside an outer step, context or batch is used). Heuristic part: N = 1,512,538 * 2^80 = 2^100.53 trials.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with 64 registers; seven trials per word in 36-bit lanes; stage A 29 operations for every batch, stage B 73 operations for at most E_B = ceil(0.6001 * p_B * V * 2^64 * 9,363) = 2^94.6573 batches (p_B = 0.1992628, proof.md Section 8.2), stage C 112 operations for at most E_C = ceil(1.27 * N * 2^-11) = 2^89.873 batches (two count-down budget registers; a spent budget halts the run with failure; stages B and C duplicated for each of the 83 unrolled batch positions, so an entry costs exactly 73 and 112); with the loop, the middle step (107 per X2 value), the block test (4), the table build (49 per list word, once per outer step) and the outer step with its random word (340): 5.4682 operations per trial, every executed primitive including loads, stores and random words counted as 1; step 3 runs at most once; no sorting and no lookup by value; the table has a fixed size of 5 * 9,363 words. The time bound holds for every value of the coins.

Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word per outer step (V * 2^32 words; four 32-bit words of each are used). Success probability 0.39 holds only under H1, the only heuristic, with parts (i) and (ii). The factor F = 92,675,072 = 2^26.4657 in H1 (i) is assumed; it is half of an exact model count of 185,350,144 (margin 2.000), recomputed by the shipped program's --count mode, that the organizer experiments do not measure. H1 (ii) asserts, as run averages, 0.60 times the exact model value p_B of the event that a batch enters stage B (the real share is lower because rule A clusters by context; two uniform samples of the run give 0.546 and 0.54644 of p_B) and 1.25 times the exact model rate 2^-11 of rule A with the filter. With the uniform rate the same search gives 120.96. No full collision is exhibited.

Preprocessing: a declared upper-bound charge (not a premise; H1 and the success bound do not use it) of 2^86 units (2^94.75 word operations) covers all selection of the stored constants, class, rule A, sub-class, filter and stage tests and of the order of the construction and the staged batch by c66f230d, 60f94c5c and by us, without reliance on run records (more than 2^34 times c66f230d's own estimate). Memory 2^100 bytes bounds that preprocessing by its charged work; the search itself uses under 2^21 bytes. Advice under 64 bytes.

heuristics.statement: Over the algorithm's random words (one fresh uniform 256-bit word per outer step), (i) the N = 1,512,538 * 2^80 trials of proof.md Section 4 behave, with respect to the event good (128-bit residual R = 0, rule A, and E1's c1 passes the beta filter), like independent events of probability at least F * 2^-128 each (F = 92,675,072 = 185,350,144 / 2 = 2^26.4657), to the extent that the probability that no trial is good is at most exp(-lambda) + 0.002 with lambda = N * F * 2^-128 = 0.4980001; and (ii) averaged over the V * 2^64 * 9,363 batches of the run, the probability that a batch has a trial satisfying rule A is at most 0.60 * p_B, and averaged over the N trials, the probability that a trial satisfies rule A and passes the beta filter is at most 1.25 * 2^-11, where p_B = 32,052,445,611,625 / 160,855,115,169,792 = 0.1992628 and 2^-11 are the exact values of these two stage events under the seven-word model M that gives the count of (i), with the distinct trials of a batch independent as in (i); the stage-B factor 0.60 is below 1 because rule A clusters by context, and rests on uniform samples of the run, not on M.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Section 4: lengths 55 and 63, the six constants of Fact P, the construction of Section 2, Y4 in the sub-class S8 of Section 3 (all 65,536 members per outer step and X2, in the stated order, seven per batch, 9,363 batches), the four words vc, D3.d1, S15, S9 from the outer step's own random word, vd below 1,512,538, w5 and X2 over 2^32 values each; rule A as in Lemma A; the filter (c1 AND 00098188) = 00008000. Part (ii) concerns averages over all batches and all trials of the run, not single contexts or batches.
heuristics.extrapolation: (i) From an exact count under the seven-word model M (proof.md Section 8.1): restricted to the six betas of T6, which the filter contains by Lemma B, the share of solutions of R = 0 with rule A among Y4 in S8 times 2^192 is 185,350,144 * 2^-128, an exact integer from 57 nonzero of 85 outcomes counted by carry automata in exact integer arithmetic without sampling (equal with and without rule A). The shipped program recomputes it: python3 experiments/s8stage.py --count prints N1, N3 and the part of every outcome, the six per-beta parts and the total (about 2.5 minutes). The source authors' C counter, the Python port and a separately written counter (183,119,872 for the four heaviest betas) agree exactly; a sampling estimator by their review agent gives ratio 1.0007 +- 0.0047; every member of S8 has an exact factor of at least 184.57M (all 15 betas); the full-class parts equal the published table of c66f230d; brute force at 8-bit words agrees on every outcome, member split and rule split. On real trials, rule-A and filter rates agree with the model at rates 2^-5 to 2^-11, the E1 part has real/model 1.0086 over 2^33.8 trials, and E3 partial events of probability about 2^-38 show the counter's S8-versus-rest ratios (1, 2.333, 7) on real trials as on model draws. F is exactly half of the count. (ii) Under M, h1 and c1 are independent uniform words; rule A holds for 2^27 of 2^32 words h1 and the filter for 2^26 of 2^32 words c1, so rule A with the filter has rate exactly 2^-11, and a batch of seven (last batch: two) distinct independent trials has a rule-A trial with probability 1 - (31/32)^7 (1 - (31/32)^2), giving p_B (--count enumerates the patterns and prints these integers and the fraction p_B). A preregistered uniform sample of the run (proof.md Section 8.2; 16,384 outer steps with vd, w5, coins and 256 values of X2 drawn uniformly, all S8 members, 2^38 trials; its counts equal the shipped program's forward computation and batching on two full drawn contexts) gives, per outer step, a stage-B batch share of 0.54629 +- 0.00047 of p_B (99.9% upper bound 0.5477 against 0.60) and a rule-A-and-filter rate of 1.00001 +- 0.00009 of 2^-11 (upper bound 1.0003 against 1.25); per run of 1,024 outer steps 0.543 to 0.550 and 0.9993 to 1.0007. An earlier run-layout sample with consecutive indices (2^38 trials: 0.510 and 1.00001), a review-agent uniform sample (2^35: 0.547 and 0.99978) and the 41 class-filter replays (0.566 +- 0.008 and 0.94 +- 0.05) agree. An independent preregistered uniform sample made for the promoted source (proof.md Section 8.3; its own C program, cross-checked against a forward 2-round compression and verifier/blake3.py on three complete contexts; 65,536 outer steps with vd, w5, coins and 128 values of X2 drawn uniformly, all S8 members, 2^39 trials) gives a stage-B batch share of 0.54644 +- 0.00023 of p_B per outer step (empirical Bernstein bound 0.5567 at delta = 2^-64, against 0.60) and rule A with the filter at 0.99995 +- 0.00007 of 2^-11 (the bounds for variables in [0, 1] are not informative for this rare event at this sample size; the stage-C part is unchanged from 098e66f4). By the lower-tail Chernoff bound proved in proof.md (Lemma C'), a run average of 0.60 p_B or more would give a sample mean this low with probability below 3 * 10^-14. For the stage-C part the extrapolation is from the exact model value with these checks; for the stage-B part it is from uniform samples of the run's own index space to the average over all 2^97.7 batches of the run.
heuristics.limitations: The factor of (i) is assumed, set at exactly half of a model count that organizer experiments do not measure (margin 2.000). M is untested at probability 2^-100.5; real trials were compared with it for events down to about 2^-38 per trial (E1 part, E3 partial events) and about 2^-40 for one call in c66f230d; the full E3 event has too few hits at our sample size to test (real 0.80 +- 0.20, model draws 0.51 +- 0.15 with the same estimator). M fails inside one context for rule A (clustering); only averages over contexts are measured, and part (ii) and Theorem 2 use only such averages. The clustering makes the real stage-B batch share about 0.55 of p_B on average, while single contexts reach 1.13 p_B and single outer steps 0.85 p_B; (ii) bounds only the run average. The constants, class and rule A were chosen by c66f230d to maximize a count of this kind; S8 is the best under M of 8,992,320 sub-classes given by three one- or two-bit conditions on e1 and supplies a factor 1.29 of the margin (if its advantage under M were entirely a selection artifact, S8 trials would have the class rate, and the full class with rule A counts 1.555 F >= F); the filter was chosen to contain the heaviest betas; choices that are best under M may favour parameters where M overstates. 37% of the S8 count (44% in the full class) comes from one beta, 18b0e098. Trials of one outer step share its four coin words and trials of one context differ only in Y4; for (i) their independence is assumed. Part (ii) is estimated from uniform samples of 2^38 (098e66f4) and 2^39 (the promoted source) trials, not from the 2^100.5 of the run, and only on the participant side; the organizer experiments see the stage events in 16,128 clustered lanes per run (41 replays: rule A alone 1.023 +- 0.016 of 2^-5, not part of (ii)). The batch-level form of the stage-B part was chosen after a first measurement had shown the share at 0.51 of p_B; its margin 1.01 and the budget 1.02 were kept from the first build, and the stage-C margin was widened from 1.01 to 1.25; the uniform sample was preregistered after these changes and is reported in full, with one malformed-seed run (proof.md Section 8.2) (all in 098e66f4). In the promoted source the stage-B factor 0.60 (budget 0.61) was chosen after reading 098e66f4's uniform sample (0.546 p_B) and before the promoted source's own sample, whose plan fixed the value and the rule to change nothing unless its empirical Bernstein bound was at most 0.60; the margin over the observed means is about 1.10, much smaller than the 1.85 of 098e66f4's 1.01 p_B. Both samples use seeded deterministic generators and run on the participant side only; the promoted source did not rerun the self-test (its program differs from 098e66f4's only in two ledger constants and docstring credit lines; both organizer experiments were rerun on the public seed through the repository's Docker runner with results identical to 098e66f4's). This derivative changes only one further ledger constant and does not claim new evidence for H1. The count program runs on the participant side (about 2.5 minutes), not as an organizer experiment. Run selection: no organizer-run count or frequency supports F or the averages of (ii); the experiments' predictions are exact per-seed predicates, every recorded replay of the promoted source is reported (proof.md Section 6: 41 participant-run local replays with program, harness and nonces hashed before running, repeated with identical results for the revised program), and no parameter, version, seed or nonce was chosen on replay outcomes.
